title: Harness
explainer: How agents are set up to work in this repository
sentence: This repository speaks to agents through {documents, plural, one {# document} other {# documents}} and has {checks, plural, one {# check} other {# checks}} in place.
structureSentence: This repository fills {filled} of the {total} places a harness has.
checksBreakdown: {hooks, plural, one {# hook script} other {# hook scripts}} · {gitHooks, plural, one {# file under .githooks/} other {# files under .githooks/}} · {scripts, plural, one {# package.json script} other {# package.json scripts}}
checksHint: "Checks" counts declarations, not distinct guards: a hook mirrored for Claude Code and for Codex is two scripts for one guard, .githooks/ holds helper modules beside its hooks, and the script list includes watch mode and the lanes a single run re-runs. What it counts is hook scripts a config names that exist on disk, files under .githooks/, and package.json lint, typecheck and test scripts. Whether any of them runs, or has ever caught anything, is not something we can know from files.
guidesTitle: Guides: what the agents were told
guidesCaption: Documents an agent reads before it starts work. Each tool reads a different set.
columnChangedHint: When the file was last modified on this disk. Not a commit date: a fresh copy stamps every file with the time it arrived.
toolsUncitedHint: Which tool reads which file comes from that tool's documentation, not from this repository. This row has no document behind it.
capMerged: Codex reads the root AGENTS.md merged with the nested AGENTS.md on the working path, and silently truncates the merge past the cap. The bar measures the merged length.
pairCompared: {count, plural, one {# reference pair compared} other {# reference pairs compared}}
pairHint: Compares same-named Codex and Claude guidance for reference. Tool-specific instructions may differ; a content difference is not an error or a requirement to synchronize them.
driftTitle: {count, plural, one {# content difference} other {# content differences}}
hooksCaption: Not a rule in prose: code that actually blocks or records.
hookWiredHint: The script the config names exists on disk. Whether it runs is not something we can know from files.
hookMissingHint: The config names this path and the file is not there. That produces no error and no block: the guard you counted on is silently absent.
hookUnresolvedHint: The command is not a script path, so we could not ask whether a file exists.
hookApprovalGateHint: Codex hashes every hook entry and will not run a new or changed one until a person trusts it in /hooks. That approval lives in no file, so we cannot read it.
browserOnlyBody: Most harness files live in dot directories: .claude, .agents, .codex. A browser's folder permission cannot see those entries at all, so a list drawn here would show far fewer files than exist. The desktop app reads all of them.
diagramSelectPart: Select a part to trace its source
diagramHint: Select a part to open the files behind it.
noSourceBody: The harness belongs to the repository agents actually edit. Connect a source folder to a project and this list fills in. When more than one folder is connected we do not pick which harness you meant.
emptyBody: There is no AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules here. Agents start on this repository having been told nothing about it.
coverageTableCaption: Domains of this repository, and what tells, gates and watches each one.
coverageColumnToldHint: Guides whose declared path scope reaches a path the ontology records for this domain: a nested AGENTS.md governing its folder, or a .claude rule whose paths: list matches. A file is here because a glob reaches it, never because a tool probably reads it.
coverageColumnGatedHint: Hook scripts a config names that exist on disk, and files under .githooks/, whose own text names a path in this domain. It says the script is there. Whether it runs, or ever blocked anything, is not readable from files.
coverageColumnWatchedHint: package.json lint, typecheck and test scripts, and CI jobs whose own path filter names a path in this domain. A check that has never caught anything cannot tell you whether the code is safe or the check is blind.
coverageEveryAreaCaption: Declares no path, so it reaches all of them. Listed once instead of in every row.
coverageCapabilityCount: {count, plural, one {# recorded path} other {# recorded paths}}
coverageRule: A file appears in a domain when a path it declares reaches a path the ontology records for that domain. Open a cell to see the declaration it came from.
coverageUnreached: {count, plural, one {# recorded path is} other {# recorded paths are}} reached by no path-scoped guide: {paths}. The always-loaded rules still reach them.
coverageOutside: {count, plural, one {# check or gate names} other {# checks and gates name}} a folder the ontology records no path in: {folders}.
coveragePathless: {count, plural, one {# capability records} other {# capabilities record}} no implementation path, so nothing here can reach it.
coverageNoAreasTitle: This repository has agent files and no ontology yet
coverageNoAreasBody: The matrix puts this repository's own domains on its rows, and those come from the ontology: a domain a person defined, with the implementation path each of its capabilities points at. Without them there is nothing to be told, gated or watched about. {documents, plural, one {# guide document was} other {# guide documents were}} still found, and the Guides view lists every one. Define a domain with a capability that carries a path, and the rows appear.
reachTotal: {total, plural, one {# authored Markdown file} other {# authored Markdown files}} · {excluded, plural, =0 {nothing excluded} one {# folder excluded} other {# folders excluded}}
reachNamedBody: A guide names this path, or a document a guide names does. Reached when it is needed.
reachUnnamedBody: On disk, and no chain of citations from any guide reaches it. An agent will not open these.
reachRule: Counted by citation, not by glob: a rule's paths: list says when to load that rule, not which documents to read. Excluded are the ontology folder and the folders this repository's own .gitignore marks as generated. Nothing else is filtered: a sample ontology folder or an archive belongs in the third row, and which of those should be unreferenced is yours to judge. A named design file is a reference, never proof the agent saw the design.
reachTruncated: The walk stopped at its bound, so these counts are a floor rather than a total.
coverageOpenNames: {column} for {area}: {count, plural, =0 {nothing names this domain} one {# declaration} other {# declarations}}
coverageEverywhereBody: Declares no path, so it applies everywhere. Listed once here instead of in all {areas} rows. It is also why an empty cell above reads “nothing names this domain” rather than “nothing runs over it”.
coverageDiscoveredTests: {count, plural, =0 {No test file sits under its recorded paths either.} one {# test file sits under its recorded paths and runs under the repository-wide lanes.} other {# test files sit under its recorded paths and run under the repository-wide lanes.}}
reachMirroredLabel: the Codex copy of a declared pair
anatomyCaption: Guidance, gates and checks found in the repository's files, placed by how they relate to an agent's work. Counts are recorded parts, not runs or scores.
anatomyProvenance: Four public sources name roughly the same parts. Fowler and Böckeler, “Harness engineering for coding agent users”, split guides from sensors. arXiv 2609.00006, “Harness Engineering: Anatomy, Architecture, and Evolution of Coding Agents” (CC BY 4.0), counts seven subsystems: agent loop, model integration, tools, memory and context, safety and permissions, orchestration, extensibility. OpenAI’s “Harness engineering” and the Codex AGENTS.md guide describe the instruction chain merged root-down, and Anthropic’s “Effective harnesses for long-running agents” describes what carries work across context windows. Five of the seven are countable from a checkout. The loop and the model are not.
anatomyTellsCaption: What an agent reads or is handed before it touches anything.
anatomyGatesCaption: What actually stops it, rather than asking it to behave.
anatomyWatchesCaption: What runs afterwards. None of it blocks.
anatomyToolCaption: The centre of a harness, and unreadable from this folder. Left blank because the answer is elsewhere, not because nothing is there.
anatomyApprovalGate: Hooks in {config} run only once a person has trusted them inside the tool. That approval lives in no file, so it cannot be read here.

always.title: Read every time
always.body: Guides an agent reads before it starts. Anything not here, it has to go and find.

scoped.title: Attached by path
scoped.body: Guides that join only when a file in their folder is touched. This is how the always-read set stays short.

tools.title: Tools it can reach
tools.body: Servers this repository wires up over the agent connection (MCP). This is the reach an agent has.

toolGates.title: Refuses a tool call
toolGates.body: Hooks that run just before a tool call and can refuse it. It says the script is on disk; whether it ever blocked anything is not readable from files.

permissions.title: Not allowed at all
permissions.body: Deny and ask rules in settings. They bite before a path is even resolved, and they outrank every hook.

gitGates.title: Caught at commit or push
gitGates.body: Files under .githooks/. The same gate whether a person or an agent typed the commit.

watchers.title: Watches after the fact
watchers.body: Hooks that run after a tool call or at the end of a turn. They record or warn; they do not block.

checks.title: Checks a command runs
checks.body: package.json lint, typecheck and test scripts. Declarations counted, not runs observed.

discoveredTests.title: Tests found by name
discoveredTests.body: Test files no command names, which the runner discovers and runs anyway.

loop.title: The agent loop and the model
loop.body: What gets read first, when to stop, what to drop when the context fills, which model runs: the tool decides all of it. No amount of reading this repository reveals it, and the same guides give different results in a different tool.

pipeline.title: Runs after it is pushed
pipeline.body: Files under .github/workflows/. They run after the code leaves this machine, so they catch what a local run let past.

skills.title: Skills, fetched when called
skills.body: Task write-ups that stay as names until something needs them. This is how the always-read set stays short without being shallow.

subagents.title: Sub-agents sent out
subagents.body: Briefs for workers that run on their own context. A Codex and a Claude copy of one name count once.

blind.title: Kept out of the agent’s view
blind.body: Files that say what an agent must not look at. A repository can write one; whether the tool honours it is the tool’s business.
blind.hintLabel: Each product uses a different file name
blind.hint: Cursor reads `.cursorignore` and `.cursorindexingignore`, Windsurf `.codeiumignore`, Gemini Code Assist `.aiexclude`, the Gemini command-line tool (CLI) `.geminiignore`, JetBrains `.aiignore`. JetBrains also honours the first three at a repository root. There is no `.claudeignore`: Claude Code uses `.gitignore` for discovery and its settings’ deny list for the rest. `.agentignore` is a proposal, not a standard.

anatomyAlwaysWeightHint: These files are read before the agent has seen a line of code, on every turn, in every session, whatever the tool. A count cannot say it: three 2 KB documents and three 40 KB documents are both "3", and that difference is the subject. Codex merges the root AGENTS.md with the nested file on the working path and silently truncates past its cap. Per-file sizes against that cap are in the Guides view.
anatomySilentGuards: {count, plural, one {# script this config names is not on disk} other {# scripts these configs name are not on disk}}: {scripts}. That produces no block and no error; the guard is simply absent.
anatomyChainWeight: the deepest chain, {path}, adds {size} for {total} a turn
anatomyChainWeightHint: A coding agent concatenates the AGENTS.md files it meets from the repository root down to the folder it is working in, at most one per directory, with the nearer file overriding what came before. So a turn does not have one cost per repository: it is the always-read set plus whatever that folder adds. The figure here is the deepest chain, which is the most expensive case; work in a shallower folder costs less.
